summary_html: CPS **accepts** a report for **investigation/assessment**. CAPTA sets the floor for investigation procedures; CFSR evaluates timeliness, safety, and decision quality.
authority_html:

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: S.C. v. New Jersey Department of Children and Families
key_cases.holding: The Court upheld the Department's 'not established' investigative category but required improved notice, a credible-evidence basis, and an informal opportunity to respond, while rejecting any right to a contested OAL hearing.
key_cases.relevance: S.C. describes the four possible investigative outcomes and the evidence needed for each.
key_cases.quote: We reject that due process considerations require the Department to conduct an adjudicative contested case proceeding either internally or at the Office of Administrative Law for a "not established" finding.

key_cases.holding: The Court held that a father's statement to a DYFS caseworker during a Title 9 investigation was voluntary and not the product of custodial interrogation, so it was admissible in his criminal prosecution.
key_cases.relevance: P.Z. defines the limits on caseworker questioning of a parent once an investigation is accepted.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that defendant's statement to Kobran was not coerced in violation of his Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination.

key_cases.holding: The Court held that coercive or suggestive interview techniques can so taint a child's statements that a pretrial hearing on reliability is required before the child's statements or testimony may be admitted.
key_cases.relevance: Michaels sets the standard for how children must be interviewed once an abuse investigation is accepted.
key_cases.quote: If a child's recollection of events has been molded by an interrogation, that influence undermines the reliability of the child's responses as an accurate recollection of actual events.

key_cases.case_name: Croft v. Westmoreland County Children and Youth Services
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court reversed summary judgment for the caseworker, holding that forcing a father from his home on the basis of an uncorroborated anonymous tip violated the family's constitutional right to integrity because there were no objectively reasonable grounds to suspect abuse.
key_cases.relevance: Croft confirms that investigating a family does not itself violate the right to family integrity, but acting on nothing does.
key_cases.quote: Even considered together, minor inconsistencies which provide no affirmative evidence of sexual abuse cannot alone establish the objectively reasonable grounds necessary to remove a family member from the family unit.

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediately upon receipt of the report; investigation initiated within 24 hours
timeline_requirements.starts_from: The Division's receipt of a report of child abuse or neglect
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.11; a delay in initiating the investigation is permitted only where the Division or other designated entity authorizes it at the request of a law enforcement official.

timeline_requirements.starts_from: State Central Registry assigns the CPS report to the local office for response
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Good cause must be established and an extension approved by the local office manager or designee before day 60 (CP&P-II-C-6-200).
